brand_active.question: What happened after the stale former CEO, and is there a current qualifying DM?

findings.subject: Marcin Rudzik
findings.finding: Former Brand Active CEO; publicly states he left Brand Active after completing the sale of the company to Cloudflight/Divante and remained only a minority shareholder.

findings.subject: Brand Active current company
findings.finding: Company is active in 2026; current LinkedIn/company pages show ongoing operations and named employees, but no current Owner/CEO/Managing Director/Head of Client Services was verified from surfaced public sources.

findings.subject: Piotr Chrzan
findings.finding: Current/visible Brand Active staff member and technical lead/developer in surfaced materials, but role is not in the current PL/CEE/DE qualifying DM matrix.

brand_active.why: The stale CEO is definitively no longer current. A current successor in a qualifying title was not verified; the company itself is active, so this is a succession/sourcing problem rather than inactivity or a matrix title gap.

storise.question: Does a current verifiable DM exist publicly, and if so is the issue role matching or source access?

findings.subject: Storise legal controller
findings.finding: Storise privacy policy identifies the controller as IDM, NIP 7792508107.

findings.subject: IDM ownership
findings.finding: Public Polish business-directory records for NIP 7792508107 identify the sole-proprietorship owner as Przemysław Kosior and the business as active.

findings.subject: Storise public site
findings.finding: Storise is active in Warsaw in 2026 but does not name leadership on its public About page.

storise.why: The direct ownership inference is now materially stronger: Storise's own privacy policy identifies IDM with NIP 7792508107 and explicitly says '(hereinafter: Storise)', while no separate Storise NIP/KRS surfaced in targeted public search. The remaining blocker is source-policy: current resolver rules do not explicitly define a multi-hop company-legal-identity -> registry-owner chain as a qualifying DM source.
storise.required_pre_run_check: Decide whether privacy-policy-derived brand/legal identity plus registry-owner evidence is an allowed DM source construction. Treat that as rule-level source-policy work, not a data-level substitution.

strongest_identity_evidence.interpretation: The site's own legal/privacy text explicitly uses Storise as the name for IDM in this context; no separate Storise legal entity identifier surfaced in the targeted search.

nip_krs_check.caution: This supports Storise as a brand/trading identity of the IDM sole proprietorship for the site. It does not by itself change DM source-policy.

planning.note: No clean data-level Run I is currently ready. Brand Active is parked on successor sourcing. Storise's brand/legal identity is now sufficiently supported to move the question from ownership inference to source-policy; any promotion experiment would be rule-level source-policy work.
